topic: How does the 45° scan range affect link budget calculations for edge-of-coverage users compared to broadside beams?
consensus_response: A 45° scan range introduces increased interference due to beam overlap, leading to higher signal blockage and reduced bandwidth utilization. This directly impacts link budget calculations as it requires more transmit power to compensate for signal degradation.  The resulting increase in multipath propagation effects further exacerbates the challenge, demanding sophisticated mitigation techniques like adaptive beamforming or advanced antenna structures.
reference_context: Increased interference from 45° scan range leads to higher multipath propagation and signal blockage at edge-of-coverage locations. This necessitates more transmit power to compensate for degraded link quality. Advanced antenna designs and sophisticated mitigation techniques like adaptive beamforming are crucial for managing increased interference, maintaining desired link budget capacity, and optimizing performance in dynamic environments.
